evidence.ref: .warp/tracker_adapter.py TrackerAdapter is an abstract seam: it declares the reads (list_intake_items, read_item) and writes (comment, set_status, create_or_update_epic, create_or_update_child) that intake and the mirror need, the base owns the cross-cutting logic (validation, the write audit, the fail-loud guard), and every surface primitive raises NotImplementedError so a real adapter must implement them (mirroring the env_provision.py seam pattern).
independent review confirmed a bare TrackerAdapter().comment(...) raises NotImplementedError and the base owns _require/_record/writes; part of selftest 1099 passed, 0 failed

.warp/tracker_adapter.py FakeTracker implements the seam in-memory (a dict of items/epics/comments/statuses) with no network, so intake and the mirror are gate-testable offline; imports are stdlib only (argparse/copy/json/sys).

selftest drives the FakeTracker through the full seam (list/read/comment/set_status/epic+child upsert); independent review reproduced the full surface end to end offline; part of selftest 1099 passed, 0 failed

.warp/tracker_adapter.py the seam is provider-agnostic (zero Jira/vendor/network code; a real Jira adapter is WARP-0604) and read/write separation is STRUCTURAL: every write routes through the base-owned audit (_record, surfaced by writes()) and no read touches it; reads return deep copies so a caller mutating a read cannot corrupt state.

independent review confirmed a run of reads leaves writes() and state_digest() unchanged while each write grows the audit by exactly one, all four writes call _record and no read does, and read/observe paths deep-copy; part of selftest 1099 passed, 0 failed

.warp/tracker_adapter.py idempotency the mirror relies on: set_status returns True only on a real change and False (no transition) when the target already holds; comment(id, text, key=None) posts a keyed comment at most once across repeats (keyless always appends) so at-least-once event replay is safe; create_or_update_epic/_child are upserts keyed by a stable caller identity with deterministic ids (epic:<key>, child:<epic>:<key>) so replay never forks a second epic/child.

independent review replayed a realistic at-least-once stream (each event 3x) and got one epic, one child, one keyed comment, and transitions equal to real state changes; part of selftest 1099 passed, 0 failed

.warp/tracker_adapter.py fail-loud: TrackerAdapterError (subclasses ValueError) for malformed args, TrackerItemNotFound (subclasses LookupError) for a read/write against an absent object; a selftest drives the fake through the full seam and asserts each write's observable effect and that reads reflect prior writes, non-tautologically.

independent review proved the teeth by mutation: making _record a no-op turns the audit-grew assertions RED, and making set_status always return True turns the no-op-repeat and transition-count assertions RED; part of selftest 1099 passed, 0 failed

assumptions: W3 of PLAN-0006: the provider-agnostic tracker adapter seam plus a deterministic in-memory FakeTracker for offline gate tests; a real Jira adapter is WARP-0604, intake WARP-0604, the mirror WARP-0605+. Pure stdlib, no network. Built by a worktree-isolated build worker and landed to main by fast-forward (main had not advanced); the independent review binds to the build commit 0107b0b. Accepted non-blocking review notes: comment's optional key param is mandated by AC4 (key-idempotency), not a vendor leak, and defaults to plain append; the epic/child audit detail logs only the key, not the applied status/title (minor observability, the audit still proves the write and read-purity); the spec is at status ready in the build commit and flips to shipped in this evidence commit, the established two-commit convention.
